Senses.Explanation: The three vehicles and twelve divisions of the teaching. Linji Yixuan quizzes a visiting Hundred Dharmas lecturer — one man gains clarity in the canon and one does not: are they the same or different? — and when the lecturer answers in doctrine, his attendant Luopu shouts the whole question off the floor; Zhaozhou Congshen tells his assembly he receives people with the fundamental matter alone, and were he to stoop to their capacity the canon would already have received them, so if they still do not understand, whose fault is it; Yunmen Wenyan grants that the canon speaks sideways and every old monk crosswise, then demands someone bring him the truth in a needle-tip of speech — calling this itself only a dead horse cured, for few ever reach that realm; and Huitang Zuxin instructs that the ancestor came only to point straight at mind, establishing no words, the canon down to its last division being yellow leaves forged into gold coins, an expedient to stop an infant's crying. Yuanwu Keqin invokes Yunmen's ruling in his commentary — were this matter in words and phrases, the canon would hardly be without speech, so why the transmission outside the teaching, why Bodhidharma from the west; Dahui Zonggao, retelling the arm-severing audience in a general discourse, has the Second Patriarch exhaust the canon and thereby know this thing cannot be sought with mind or no-mind, before asking Bodhidharma to settle his mind; Wu'an Puning narrates that after the nirvana the great disciples from Kasyapa and Ananda compiled the forty-nine years of teaching into the canon, filling not only the dragon palace but the ocean treasury; Gulin Qingmao, at the seedling festival, rules that gone the ancestor's way, the canon with bodhi and nirvana is pierced through top to bottom, or else he will open the expedient gate and show a second-meaning message; Zhongfeng Mingben writes to a Yunnan lecturer that the canon prescribing by illness and matching capacity is itself the skillful means, as are the seventeen hundred stale koans and all the sages' diverse buddha-work; and Chushi Fanqi brands the whole canon as much like a manure pit, demands why they poke their heads into it, and invites them to tangle — where every buddha and old monk loses tongue and blade.
